findings: The future binding requires actual prepared files, exact source and CPU report identities, final new128 audit/checkpoint hashes, and a passed review of the exact actual plan. It cannot bind a used execution directory or a provisional checkpoint.
Every one of 66 velocity files is checked against exact names, shape, FP32 dtype, finite values, file hash, tensor hash and reconstructed noise/time/context/command identity.

All 12 held-out score groups, six separate seen506 losses and three original999 contrasts are recomputed from raw arrays. The copied reader preserves FP32 CFG operation order and future-only FP64 score formulas.

The numerical gate requires improvement over zero and old128 plus positive alignment on all four held-out noises. It remains separate from artifact status and descriptive FP64 serialization tolerance.

The 12 original0/original128 comparisons use observed objective-* and causal-* filenames with exact old input and prediction hashes. Equality and magnitudes are descriptive, with no added cross-run acceptance tolerance.
The original 900-second, host/CUDA caps and free-memory floors remain enforced. Sequential allocated/reserved mismatches are reported without imposing an extra instantaneous relation.
No concrete source or runtime-report mismatch found against the frozen assessment producer.
limitations: Source review and seven retained author CPU cases only; no actual new assessment output is available yet.
Saved outputs and source/counter records support the declared 12 feature extractions; the auditor does not replay foundation features.
